arguments.quote: tomli is a tiny backport with the same API, and we only need it on Python older than 3.11.
arguments.text: It can be read with standard library support or a small backport.

alternatives.description: Using TOML within pyproject.toml for configuration.
alternatives.status_quote: Decision: we will read a [tool.quillfmt] table from pyproject.toml using tomllib, with tomli on older Pythons.
alternatives.title: TOML inside pyproject.toml

arguments.quote: YAML worries me. Its implicit typing means a value like no silently becomes false, and we would need PyYAML as a new runtime dependency.
arguments.text: Implicit typing causes silent errors and requires an extra dependency.

alternatives.description: Using a dedicated YAML file for configuration.
alternatives.status_quote: YAML is rejected because of the implicit typing surprises and the extra dependency.
alternatives.title: YAML file

arguments.quote: INI through configparser is in the standard library, so it costs zero dependencies.
arguments.text: It uses the standard library's configparser.

arguments.quote: INI cannot express nested tables or lists cleanly. Our per-language overrides need nesting, so INI would force awkward dotted keys.
arguments.text: It cannot handle the required nested structure for overrides.

alternatives.description: Using the INI file format for configuration.
alternatives.status_quote: INI is rejected because it cannot express nested overrides.
alternatives.title: INI file

arguments.quote: Executing user Python just to read configuration is a security risk when quillfmt runs in CI on untrusted pull requests. I am against it.
arguments.text: Executing user Python is a security risk in CI environments.

alternatives.description: Using a plain Python file to store configuration dynamically.
alternatives.status_quote: I withdraw the Python config file idea.
alternatives.title: quillfmt_config.py (Plain Python file)

arguments.quote: Could we also support a standalone .quillfmt.toml file for repositories that are not Python projects?
arguments.text: It allows configuration outside of Python projects.

alternatives.description: Supporting a standalone TOML file for repositories not in Python projects.
alternatives.status_quote: let's postpone the standalone .quillfmt.toml file until after 1.0, because it needs its own file discovery rules.
alternatives.title: Standalone .quillfmt.toml file

arguments.quote: JSON has no comments, which is painful for configuration files people edit by hand.
arguments.text: It lacks comments, which is inconvenient for manual editing.

arguments.quote: True, although JSON5 would fix that. I have no strong opinion.
arguments.text: JSON5 could potentially resolve the comment issue.

alternatives.description: Supporting JSON as a configuration format.
alternatives.title: JSON configuration

arguments.quote: Environment overrides would be handy in CI.
arguments.text: It is useful for CI overrides.

alternatives.description: Allowing environment variables to override file settings.
alternatives.title: Environment variables for overrides
